messages:
andrew: quick note — ran a targeted microbench on the rtx-6k pool comparing unified-batcher (prefill+decode in one queue) vs split-path (separate queues + handshake).
jess: nice, what metrics did you look at?
andrew: p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, kernel hotpath time, token-cost per request. test harness: 1k concurrent short prompts (avg 40 tokens prefill, 20 decode), 90s steady-state.
kai: aha — what's the difference in batch formation behavior?
andrew: unified tends to form mixed-phase batches which forces kernel to pick a gen-optimized path with larger kv loads; split keeps prefill-only batches smaller, letting prefill use dense matmul kernel.
maria: results?
andrew: split-path: p95 down ~80ms on avg across runs, p50 similar. cost per token +1.7% on split because smaller prefill batches reduce batching efficiency; but overall tail latency improved and fewer kv thrash events.
linh: can you paste the profiling snippet?
andrew: sure:
```
kernel_times: {
  attention_custom: 42.1%,
  matmul_dense: 28.3%,
  kv_copy: 12.4%,
  other: 17.2%
}
p95_latency: unified=320ms, split=240ms
gpu_util: unified=78%, split=66%
kv_evictions/sec: unified=4.8, split=1.2
```
jess: kv_evictions that big explains tail. are we priming KV differently?
andrew: test used no explicit KV priming; split lets prefill warm local kv cache before decode bursts, so decode sees fewer misses.
kai: what about the kernel selector? did it choose quantized kernels differently?
andrew: yes — unified batches often choose the quant+fallback path due to mixed shapes; split allows a deterministic quant path for prefill and a narrower gen path for decode. that reduced attention_custom stalls.
maria: any regressions observed outside tail? CPU jitter?
andrew: observed a regression in token throughput for long-seq workloads ~2.1% due to smaller prefill microbatches. it's workload-dependent.
linh: did you try token_budget knobs?
andrew: ran grid: token_budget={32,64,96,128} with prefill_max_seqs={4,8,16}. sweet spot seems token_budget=64 + prefill_max_seqs=8 for our short-prompt mix: good tail vs acceptable cost.
perf-bot: perf alert: split-path experiment reduces p95 25% but increases avg-cost-per-token 1.9% in baseline workload (annotated).
jess: thanks — we should capture this as a scheduler feature flag. propose: phase_aware=true with defaults token_budget=64, prefill_limit=8, decode_limit=32.
kai: add a safemode: if gpu_util < 50% then relax prefill_limit to 16 to regain throughput.
maria: also add telemetry counters: kv_miss_rate, kernel_choice, batch_shape_histogram so we can A/B.
linh: agree. can we simulate enterprise traffic (longer prefill, streaming decode) before rolling?
andrew: yes — I'll run a 30m soak with mixed tails and attach perf traces. will open an RFC with config sketch and flame graphs.
jess: awesome. next steps: andrew run soak + push draft RFC; kai implement flag + safemode; maria add telemetry; linh run enterprise soak.
andrew: on it. attaching quick command for replicate run:
```
./bench_runner --cluster rtx-6k --clients 1000 --prefill_tokens 40 --decode_tokens 20 --duration 90 --mode split-path --tbudget 64 --prefill_max_seqs 8
```
linh: ping me when you have flame graphs. also add the kv_cache latency heatmap to the RFC.
andrew: will do. :thumbsup:
